synopsis: Great Britain’s Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008, as amended, impose general machinery safety and conformity obligations; SI 2026/867 amendments take effect on 20 January 2027 [f2218, f2758, f15490]. The EN 474:2022 earth-moving machinery family was designated by a notice dated 8 August 2026, providing a presumption-of-conformity route, but the attributed notice number 0139/26 was not confirmed [f15244, f2875]. This designation is not an automatic-braking performance matrix: the booklet found neither a dedicated Great Britain off-road automatic-braking test regime nor a UK collision-avoidance mandate, with the latter explicitly framed as an expert-opinion planning caution [f2222, f2219, f2227]. The program needs a parallel British declaration path and standards-designation calendar; Great Britain has UKCA and approved bodies, whereas Northern Ireland remains under EU product law, so one declaration route should not be assumed to cover both [f15496, f15110, f15494]. HSE figures report 126 worker deaths in Great Britain in 2025/26, including 24 deaths from moving vehicles, the second most common cause; guidance attributes nearly a quarter of workplace-transport deaths to reversing and 40% of quarry accidents and 60% of quarry deaths to transport [f15498, f15499, f15500, f15501]. These figures support the system’s harm-prevention rationale, but the booklet did not verify the Quarries Regulations 1999 or relevant HSE and industry guidance in its UK regulatory review [f15503, f2225, f2226, f15502].
